# Aletheia

> Aletheia (npm package aletheia-mem) is a free, local memory and rules hub for AI coding tools such as Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Windsurf and OpenCode. One SQLite store is read over MCP, REST or CLI. Apache-2.0, no account, no telemetry. Alpha status.

Aletheia is a small server, a command line tool and an MCP server over one local SQLite file. Hooks in each AI coding tool capture sessions, secrets are redacted before storing, and the next session gets the relevant context back. Rules are written once and synced into each tool's own instruction file. Every page below is plain Markdown. Real-tool verification is stated per tool; answer accuracy is not measured.

## Get started

- [Introduction to Aletheia, a local memory hub for AI coding tools](https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/start/introduction.md): Aletheia (aletheia-mem) is a free, local memory and rules hub that gives AI coding tools persistent memory over MCP, REST and a CLI.
- [Install Aletheia with npm, git or Docker](https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/start/installation.md): Install Aletheia (aletheia-mem) with npm, git or Docker, start the server on port 37790, set up auto-start, update it and remove it. Needs Bun 1.1+.
- [Quickstart: save, search and recall a memory with Aletheia](https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/start/quickstart.md): A ten-minute path through Aletheia (aletheia-mem): start the server, save and search memories, print session context, add a rule, preview the installer.
- [How Aletheia works: capture, redact, store, compress, recall](https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/start/how-it-works.md): How Aletheia (aletheia-mem) turns hook events into memory: capture, redaction, SQLite storage, queued fact extraction and session-start context.
- [The Aletheia dashboard: five tabs for memory, rules and tools](https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/start/dashboard.md): A tour of the Aletheia (aletheia-mem) dashboard: what Home, Activity, Knowledge, Rules and Connections show, and what you can change in each.
- [Aletheia FAQ: memory, privacy, tools and limits](https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/start/faq.md): Short answers about Aletheia (aletheia-mem): cost, data location, privacy, which tools it connects to, deleting memory, offline use and its alpha status.

## Concepts

- [Aletheia memory model: memories, facts, episodes and rules](https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/concepts/memory-model.md): What Aletheia stores in hub.db: memory kinds and types, facts, episodes, entities, rules, project and global scope, pin, dismiss and importance.
- [Rules: write standing instructions once and sync them to every tool](https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/concepts/rules.md): How Aletheia rules work: scopes, enabled, stale, confirm and retire, the managed block in each tool file, preview, diff, lint, sync and import.
- [Search: keyword, project scope and optional semantic search](https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/concepts/search.md): How Aletheia search works: FTS5 keyword search, project scope and --scope all, --explain, optional semantic search, ranking and the agent search pattern.
- [Session-start context: what a new AI session receives](https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/concepts/session-context.md): What the Aletheia session-start block holds: the day-grouped index, legend, fetch hint, token estimate, the context.facts setting and how to shrink it.
- [Privacy and redaction in Aletheia](https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/concepts/privacy.md): What Aletheia stores and where, which secrets it redacts and which it misses, how private blocks work, what can leave your machine, and how to erase data.
- [33. Facts](https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/33-facts.md): Facts are the atomic, declarative pieces of memory that sit under summaries, search and the session-start context. They are extracted from captured memory, never from a model's ...
- [Aletheia glossary: terms used in the documentation](https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/concepts/glossary.md): Plain definitions of the terms used in the Aletheia docs: memory, observation, fact, episode, rule, hook, host, hub, spool, redaction, FTS5, MCP and more.

- [Claude Desktop and the aletheia MCP server](https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/claude-desktop.md): Claude Desktop speaks MCP over stdio. Aletheia's server is bin/mcp.mjs; one JSON entry under mcpServers is all it needs. No hook and no rules file exist for Claude Desktop, so t...

## Guides

- [Migrate from claude-mem to Aletheia](https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/guides/migrate-from-claude-mem.md): Import your claude-mem observations, summaries and prompts into Aletheia, run both side by side, switch the Claude Code hook and roll back.
- [Write your AI coding rules once and sync them to every tool](https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/guides/write-rules-once.md): Add rules once in Aletheia, preview the change, lint them, and write them into CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and other tool files with a backup.
- [Back up, export and move Aletheia memory between machines](https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/guides/backup-export-import.md): Export Aletheia memory and rules as JSONL or Markdown, copy hub.db safely with its WAL files, import on another machine, and erase with a receipt.
- [Run Aletheia as a background service (systemd, launchd, Docker)](https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/guides/run-as-a-service.md): Generate a systemd user unit or a macOS launchd plist for the Aletheia server, set CPU and memory limits, read logs, upgrade, or run it in Docker.
- [Model providers: none, Claude CLI, OpenAI-compatible and Ollama](https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/guides/model-providers.md): Choose how Aletheia extracts facts: rule-based with no model, the Claude CLI, an OpenAI-compatible API or Ollama, plus env vars and privacy notes.
- [Troubleshooting Aletheia: port in use, MCP closed, no memories and more](https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/guides/troubleshooting.md): Fix common Aletheia problems: EADDRINUSE, MCP CONNECTION_CLOSED, an old dashboard, E404 on install, missing memories, locked or corrupt database.
- [29. Aletheia Sync](https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/29-sync.md): Status: implemented, 2026-10-26. This page describes the code that exists.
- [30. The private remote MCP endpoint](https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/30-remote-mcp.md): Status: implemented, 2026-10-26. This page describes the code that exists and is tested by test/remote-mcp.test.mjs.
- [31. Team mode](https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/31-team.md): Status: implemented and tested, 2026-10-26. This page describes what the code does. It does not claim SSO, SCIM, compliance certificates or an SLA; none of those are built.
- [32. Requests, goals, story and economics](https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/32-requests.md): Status: implemented, 2026-10-27. This page describes the code that exists: src/hub/requests.mjs, goals-rollup.mjs, artifacts.mjs, story.mjs, economics.mjs, rule-suggest.mjs, rul...

## Reference

- [Aletheia CLI reference: every aletheia command and flag](https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/reference/cli.md): Every aletheia command and flag with a synopsis and a real example: capture, search, rules, install, sync, team, service, erase and alerts.
- [MCP tools reference: the 13 Aletheia MCP tools and their inputs](https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/reference/mcp-tools.md): The 13 tools the Aletheia MCP server lists, with input schemas, read or write access, example calls and results, plus stdio and HTTP setup.
- [Aletheia configuration reference: environment variables, settings and data directory](https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/reference/configuration.md): Every Aletheia environment variable with its default, the runtime settings and where they are stored, and the files in the data directory.
- [Aletheia hooks reference: events, payloads, redaction and fail-open behavior](https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/reference/hooks.md): How Aletheia hooks work: events per host, payload fields read, redaction, fail-open exit 0, the spool, timeouts, and how to test or remove a hook.
- [3. HTTP API](https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/03-http-api.md): Base: http://127.0.0.1:<port>. All JSON responses carry Cache-Control: no-store. Pages carry Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none' and X-Frame-Options: DENY.
